sections.title: A World-Class Education at an Exceptional Value
sections.intro: Austria combines high academic standards with an enviable quality of life. Situated at the centre of Europe, it offers international students rigorous research environments and tuition costs that compare favourably with other global study hubs.

items.title: Outstanding affordability
items.desc: Public university tuition remains exceptionally modest (≈ €726.72/semester), even for international students from outside the EU/EEA.

items.title: Academic and professional depth
items.desc: Austrian universities are globally recognized in engineering, business, computer science, natural sciences, music, medicine and the arts.

items.title: Exceptional quality of life
items.desc: Vienna is consistently ranked among the #1 most liveable cities in the world, while Graz, Innsbruck and Linz offer vibrant student alternatives.

items.title: A route to a career in Europe
items.desc: Graduates may apply for the Red-White-Red Card to seek skilled employment, with degrees fully portable across Europe.

items.title: A European gateway
items.desc: Situated in the heart of Europe, Austria provides immediate access to Germany, Switzerland, Italy, and Central European business hubs.

sections.title: Distinguished Institutions in Austria
sections.intro: The following institutions represent key destinations available to EUROPA FUSION students.

items.name: University of Vienna
items.desc: Austria’s largest and oldest university, offering an exceptionally wide spectrum of disciplines across sciences, humanities, law and economics.

items.name: TU Wien
items.desc: A premier European centre for engineering, computer science, architecture and mathematics, with close ties to Austrian industry.

items.name: WU Vienna (Vienna University of Economics & Business)
items.desc: One of Europe’s foremost triple-accredited business universities, recognized internationally for management, finance and business law.

items.name: TU Graz
items.desc: Distinguished in engineering and natural sciences, with strong industry partnerships in automotive mobility, energy and semiconductors.

items.name: University of Graz
items.desc: A comprehensive research university known for law, social sciences, natural sciences, biotechnology and sustainability research.

items.name: University of Innsbruck
items.desc: Renowned for physics, alpine and climate research, environmental sciences, sports science, medicine and the humanities.

items.name: Johannes Kepler University Linz (JKU)
items.desc: Combines cutting-edge technology, artificial intelligence, software engineering, business and law within an innovation-focused campus.

items.name: MCI | The Entrepreneurial School
items.desc: A practice-oriented institution offering management, entrepreneurship, technology and tourism programmes with direct employer links.

sections.title: Programmes and Qualifications in Austria
sections.intro: Austrian higher education follows the Bologna three-cycle model with public universities, Fachhochschulen (FH), and medical diplomas.
rows: Requires recognised Matura equivalent; wide range of German-taught programmes and selective English options.

Medicine (MedAT entrance test), Dentistry and Law; integrated single-cycle professional degrees.
Research-intensive study, often with salaried employment-style contracts at the university or research institutes.
Practice-oriented study with mandatory industry internships; selective entry with tests or interviews.
Smaller cohorts and high faculty ratio; English-taught programmes with institution-set tuition fees.

items.desc: Courses are matched to your profile, with attention to language of instruction, admission procedures and deadlines.

items.title: Documents & application
items.desc: Transcripts, certificates, language proof, CV, motivation letter and passport are prepared and submitted directly or via portals.

items.desc: Where required, preparation for entrance tests, interviews, or Austrian foundation-course (Vorstudienlehrgang) prerequisites.

items.desc: Preparation of the Austrian Student Residence Permit (Aufenthaltsbewilligung Student) file, including proof of funds and accommodation.

items.title: Arrival & settling in

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.intro: Common questions about studying and settling in Austria.

items.q: Can I study in Austria in English?
items.a: Yes. Austria offers a growing number of English-taught Master’s programmes, particularly in technology, business, economics and the sciences. Most Bachelor’s programmes at public universities are taught in German, so the language of instruction must be confirmed for every course.

items.q: Do I need to know German?
items.a: For German-taught programmes, certified proficiency (such as Goethe-Zertifikat or TestDaF, typically B2 or C1) is required. For English-taught programmes it is not mandatory, but even basic German greatly improves daily life, part-time work and career prospects.

items.q: How much does it cost to study in Austria?
items.a: Austria offers some of Europe’s most reasonable tuition. Non-EU students at public universities currently pay around €726.72 per semester (≈ €1,453/year) plus a small student union (ÖH) fee. Living costs typically range between €950 and €1,300 per month.

items.q: When are the intakes and application deadlines?
items.a: The main intake is the winter semester beginning in October, with a smaller summer intake beginning in March. Non-EU applicants face earlier deadlines because the residence permit process runs in parallel, so applications should begin 9 to 12 months in advance.
Most English-taught programmes request proof of proficiency such as IELTS (6.0–7.0) or TOEFL (80–100), depending on the university and program.

items.q: How much money must I show for the residence permit?
items.a: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds for their stay. Official figures are approximately €722.58 per month for students under 24 (≈ €8,670/year) and €1,308.39 per month for students aged 24 or over (≈ €15,700/year).

items.q: Are scholarships available for international students?
items.a: Yes. Opportunities include OeAD-administered programmes, the Ernst Mach Grant, merit awards from individual universities and selected Erasmus Mundus joint Master’s programmes.

items.q: Can I work while studying in Austria?
items.a: Non-EU students may work part-time (up to 20 hours per week) subject to an employment permit (Beschäftigungsbewilligung) issued by the AMS.

items.q: Can I stay in Austria after graduating?
items.a: Graduates of Austrian universities can apply for a 12-month extension of their student residence permit to seek employment, and then transition to the Red-White-Red Card (Rot-Weiß-Rot-Karte).

Typically: passport, academic transcripts and degree certificates (with apostille/legalisation), language-test results, CV, motivation letter, proof of financial means, proof of accommodation and Austrian-compliant health insurance.

items.q: How does EUROPA FUSION support my application?
items.a: We assist at every stage: profile assessment, university shortlisting, German/English document review, entrance assessment guidance, Aufenthaltsbewilligung permit filing, and accommodation booking.
